items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: he taught me from the whole note of breathing at the end of each bar

ctx.x: He said, I've got more lip. He was another one of those jitney men. You know, he'd been there. He was on the jitney a long time with Earl Foster too. Right over there on the canal at the Alamo. Yeah, that was before Alvin Alcorn went in there. He went and got young this day.

So far, this sounds like a trumpet lesson. There's one more question I have to ask before we move on to your life again. Did Mr. Matoy ever say anything about breathing, anything special, exercises on breathing or anything that he gave you?

Well, yeah, see, in fact, he taught me from the whole note of breathing at the end of each bar, if you can, that's where you take your breath. Unless you have a break in between the bar where you can take a breath and you're going to have a tie over to the next bar to keep you from turning that tie loose where you'll catch your breath right in between there.
